draft.title: Genre conventions
card: A genre is a group of texts that share patterns. Mystery, fantasy and science fiction are all genres.
These shared patterns are called conventions. They can be in the plot, the setting, the types of character and the language.
In a mystery, a crime is often solved by a detective who follows clues. In fantasy, a young hero often leaves home and faces magic in an invented world.
Readers learn conventions from the texts they have read. They use them to predict what will happen and to know what kind of story they are in.
draft.remember: Conventions are the shared patterns of a genre, and readers use them to predict.

opts: Patterns that texts in a genre tend to share
Rules that every text must follow exactly
The main message a writer wants to teach
The order in which a story's events happen
a.why: Conventions are shared patterns in plot, setting, characters and language. They are habits of a genre, not strict rules. The order of events is the plot, which is only one place where conventions can appear.
a.clue: Think of patterns you notice across many texts of one kind.

b.q: Sam starts a story where a body is found in a locked library and a detective arrives with a notebook. Which prediction uses genre conventions?
opts: The detective will follow clues to find who did it
A dragon will arrive and carry the detective away
The story will end with a space voyage to Mars
The library will turn out to be the hero's home
b.why: A crime, a detective and a notebook signal a mystery. In that genre, detectives usually follow clues to solve the crime. The dragon prediction belongs to fantasy, so nothing in the opening supports it.
b.clue: Which genre does a crime and a detective point to?

a.best: Patterns that texts in a genre tend to share

b.best: The detective will follow clues to find who did it
